sanskrit: tam ādatta tam ud aiṅgayat tam upāmimīta pra harāṇīti ||
english: He took it up, he shook it up, he measured it out — saying: 'Let me hurl it forth.'

sanskrit: so 'sya hastād amucyata daivo vajraḥ kṣuraḥ paviḥ sahasrapṛṣṭir divispṛśaḥ ||
english: It slipped from his hand — the divine thunderbolt, the razor, the wheel-rim, thousand-edged, touching the sky.

sanskrit: sa saṃśiñjāno 'tiṣṭhad dhariharā bhavann etad ṛcchan ||
english: It stood there hissing, becoming tawny-gold, finding its mark.

sanskrit: sa samudraṃ prāviśat sa samudram adahat ||
english: It entered the ocean; it burned the ocean.

sanskrit: tasmāt samudro durgir apapid vaiśvānareṇa hi dagdhaḥ ||
english: Therefore the ocean swallowed its bad speech, for it had been burned by Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: sa śakra ud akrāmat so 'dhyāyad asau vajro asuraiḥ sampadyadevās taṃ rakṣati vrataṃ carāṇīti sa vratam acarat ||
english: Śakra strode out; he pondered: 'That thunderbolt has fallen in with the Asuras — the gods must protect it; let me observe the vow.' And he observed the vow.

sanskrit: so 'ṇuḥ kṛśo 'bhavat tasmād aṇuḥ kṛśo vratacārī bhavaty aṇur hi kṛśo bhūtvendro asurān apāvṛṅkta ||
english: He became thin and lean; therefore the vow-observer becomes thin and lean — for it was as a thin, lean being that Indra thrust the Asuras away.
He ran to Parameṣṭhin.
He ran to Prajāpati.
He ran to Viṣṇu.
He ran to the Lord of the House.
He ran to Virāj.
He ran to Svarāj.
He ran to Samrāj.
He ran to Day-and-Night.
He ran to the Fortnights.
He ran to the Months.
He ran to the Seasons.
He ran to the Seasonal ones.
He ran to the Seers.
He ran to the descendants of the Seers.
He ran up to Aṅgiras.
He ran to the Āṅgirasas.
He ran to Atharvan.
He ran to the Ātharvaṇas.

sanskrit: viśvān devān marudgaṇās tam anv avādravan somaḥ prathamo 'thendrāgnī ||
english: The Marut-hosts ran after him toward all the gods — Soma first, then Indra and Agni.

sanskrit: tam upāmantrayantāpuṇyayā vācā krūrayā ca haniṣyāmas tvā vittvā cetsyāmonacatamiṣyasīti so 'śāmyat ||
english: They addressed him with inauspicious and cruel speech: 'We will slay you — we know you, we will cut you off, you shall not escape.' And he became calm.

sanskrit: tasmād yo brahma vedotāpaskṛtaṃ śamayati dohayata evainān ||
english: Therefore, one who calms a brahmin who knows the Veda and has performed austerities merely milks them for benefit.

sanskrit: tam ṛksāmābhyām ādatta yajuṣā yajñena gāyatreṇa vāmadevyena ca ||
english: He took it up with Ṛk and Sāman, with Yajus and sacrifice, with the Gāyatra and the Vāmadevya.

sanskrit: etad vā idaṃ sarvaṃ yad ṛksāme etāv indrasya bāhū ||
english: All this indeed is Ṛk and Sāman — these two are the arms of Indra.
He took it up; he set it in the joints.

sanskrit: prajā vai samṛddhir akṣitiḥ paśavaḥ parūṃṣi ||
english: Offspring is indeed prosperity, inexhaustible; cattle are the joints.

sanskrit: prajām eva samṛddhim akṣitim ava rundhe yaḥ (…) || [see 17.27.4b
english: He who [performs this rite] obtains offspring, prosperity, and inexhaustible [wealth] — [see 17.27.4b].
He who [performs this rite] stands firm in all the directions.

sanskrit: sarvān eva puṇyām̐l lokān ava rundhe sarvāś ca devatā yaḥ (…) ||
english: He who [performs this rite] obtains all the auspicious worlds and all the deities.
